examples.en: The government decided to speed up the reforms.
The company sped up the development of the new product.

examples.ko: 기후 변화가 빙하가 녹는 속도를 가속화해요.
examples.en: Climate change speeds up the rate at which glaciers melt.
To speed up the schedule, we need more people.

examples.ko: 경쟁이 심해지면서 기업들이 투자를 가속화하고 있어요.
examples.en: As competition grows, companies are accelerating their investments.

examples.ko: 도시 개발을 가속화하면 환경 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If urban development is accelerated, environmental problems may arise.

explain: 개혁, 개발, 투자처럼 큰 일의 속도를 더 빠르게 만든다고 할 때 써요. 뉴스와 회의에서 많이 들리고, 일상에서는 '서두르다, 빨리하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 일이 저절로 빨라질 때는 '가속화되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when making the pace of big things like reforms, development or investment faster. You hear it often in news and meetings, while in daily life '서두르다' or '빨리하다' sounds more natural. When something speeds up on its own, people say '가속화되다'.

examples.ko: 신청 절차를 간소화해서 서류가 두 장으로 줄었어요.
examples.en: They simplified the application process, so the documents dropped to two pages.
City Hall simplified its complaint handling process.
I wish they would simplify the complicated rules.

examples.ko: 짐을 줄이려고 여행 준비를 간소화하려고 해요.
examples.en: I want to simplify my travel preparation to cut down on luggage.

examples.ko: 결혼식 절차를 간소화하는 부부가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more couples are simplifying their wedding procedures.
The company decided to simplify its approval steps.

explain: '간단하게 하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 절차, 서류, 제도처럼 단계가 있는 것에 잘 어울려요. '복잡하게 하다'와 반대이고, '절차가 간소화돼요'처럼 피동으로도 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '간단하게 하다' (make simple), but fits things with steps such as procedures, paperwork and systems. Its opposite is '복잡하게 하다', and you can also say it passively: '절차가 간소화돼요'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 고급품만 팔아서 값이 비싸요.
examples.en: This shop only sells high-end goods, so it's expensive.
I'd like to buy you a high-quality item as a gift.
It's a premium product, so it doesn't break even after long use.
There's a reason premium goods cost so much.
The department store has a separate section for luxury goods.
I prefer practical things to high-end products.

explain: '명품'은 이름난 브랜드의 물건을 말할 때 많이 쓰고, '고급품'은 품질이 좋은 물건 전체에 써요. 반대로 값싸고 질이 낮은 물건은 '저가품'이나 '싸구려'라고 해요.
explain_en: '명품' is often used for famous-brand goods, while '고급품' covers any item of good quality. The opposite is '저가품' or '싸구려' for cheap, low-quality goods.

examples.en: This app works like a map.

examples.ko: 약이 제대로 기능하지 않는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The medicine doesn't seem to be working properly.
That room also served as a study.

examples.ko: 몸의 모든 부분이 함께 기능하는 거예요.
examples.en: All parts of the body function together.
This rule will serve as a guide.
The system is functioning well, so there's no problem.

explain: 기계의 작동보다는 어떤 것이 맡은 역할을 한다는 뜻에서 자주 써요. 'A로 기능하다'는 'A 역할을 하다'와 같아요. 기계가 움직인다고 할 때는 '작동하다', '돌아가다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used more for something playing its role than for a machine running. 'Function as A' means to act in the role of A. For machines simply running, other verbs meaning 'operate' or 'run' are more common.

examples.ko: 서류 단순화 덕분에 신청이 훨씬 쉬워졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the simplified paperwork, applying became much easier.
Many people say the procedure needs to be simplified.

examples.ko: 단순화는 편리하지만 중요한 내용이 빠질 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Simplification is convenient, but important content can get left out.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 디자인 단순화로 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: This app became popular through its simplified design.
Complicated explanations need simplifying.

examples.ko: 회사는 결재 단계의 단순화를 추진하고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is pushing to simplify the approval steps.

explain: 복잡한 것을 간단하게 만드는 일이에요. '간소화'는 절차를 줄여서 간단히 한다는 느낌으로 행정 뉴스에 자주 나오고, '단순화'는 구조나 설명을 쉽게 만들 때도 써요. 너무 단순화하면 중요한 부분이 빠질 수 있다는 뜻으로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the act of making something complicated simple. '간소화' feels like cutting down procedures and often appears in administrative news, while '단순화' is also used for making structures or explanations easier. People often use it to warn that oversimplifying can lose important parts.

examples.en: Write the correct answer inside the square brackets.
I marked the title in square brackets at the start of the sentence.
In math, you use square brackets after parentheses.
What is inside the square brackets is an explanation.

examples.ko: 인용문에 설명을 덧붙일 때 대괄호를 사용해요.
examples.en: When adding an explanation to a quotation, you use square brackets.

examples.ko: 제목 앞에 대괄호가 붙어 있어서 공지인 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: The title had square brackets in front, so I thought it was a notice.

explain: [ ] 모양의 괄호예요. ( )는 '소괄호', { }는 '중괄호'라고 해요. 게시글 제목에서 [공지]처럼 말머리를 표시할 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the bracket shaped like [ ]. ( ) is '소괄호' and { } is '중괄호'. It is also often used to mark tags on post titles, such as [공지].

examples.en: Korean words correspond to English words.

examples.ko: 표를 보면 숫자가 글자와 대응된다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you look at the table, you can see the numbers match the letters.

examples.ko: 이 말은 영어로 정확히 대응되지 않아요.
examples.en: This word doesn't have an exact English counterpart.
Find the answer that matches each question.
The colors are matched to numbers.
Connect them with a line so they correspond to each other.

explain: '대응되다'는 두 개가 서로 짝이 맞을 때 써요. '~에 대응되다'로 말하고, 번역이나 표, 문제와 답 같은 설명에 자주 나와요. 상황에 맞게 행동하는 '대응하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: 대응되다 is used when two things pair up with each other, as in '~에 대응되다'. It often appears in explanations about translation, tables, and questions and answers. It differs from 대응하다, which means to respond to a situation.

examples.ko: 두 서류의 동일성 여부를 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether the two documents are identical.

examples.ko: 이 연구는 두 집단의 동일성이 먼저 증명되어야 해요.
examples.en: For this study, the sameness of the two groups must be proven first.
It's hard to judge identity from the photo alone.

examples.ko: 문화마다 동일성보다 다양성을 중요하게 생각할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: In some cultures, diversity is considered more important than uniformity.

examples.ko: 모습이 바뀌어도 나라는 동일성은 유지된다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think my identity as myself stays the same even if my appearance changes.

examples.ko: 데이터의 동일성이 깨지면 시스템에 오류가 나요.
examples.en: If the consistency of the data breaks, the system gets errors.

explain: '같음'이나 '똑같다'보다 딱딱해서 철학, 법, 연구 글에서 많이 써요. 반대로 쓰는 말은 '다양성'이고, '동일성 여부', '동일성을 유지하다'처럼 자주 짝지어요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '같음' or '똑같다' and is common in philosophy, law and research writing. A contrasting word is '다양성' (diversity), and it often pairs as '동일성 여부' (whether it is identical) or '동일성을 유지하다' (maintain identity).

examples.ko: 이 물은 무색이라서 맛도 냄새도 없어요.
examples.en: This water is colorless, so it has no taste or smell.
I put the medicine in a colorless, transparent bottle.

examples.ko: 무색에 가까운 액체가 컵에 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: A nearly colorless liquid is in the cup.

examples.ko: 무색으로 된 유리는 빛이 잘 통해요.
examples.en: Colorless glass lets light through well.

examples.ko: 화학 시간에 무색 용액이 붉게 변하는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: In chemistry class I saw a colorless solution turn red.
Before the paint was mixed in, it was colorless glue.

explain: '무색 투명', '무색무취'처럼 굳은 표현으로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 물이나 유리를 '투명하다'고 해요. 형용사 '무색하다'는 '민망하다'에 가까운 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It appears mostly in fixed phrases like 무색 투명 and 무색무취. In everyday talk, water or glass is described as 투명하다. The adjective 무색하다 is a completely different word, closer to feeling embarrassed.

examples.ko: 이 가스는 무색무취라서 가스가 새어도 알기 어려워요.
examples.en: This gas is colorless and odorless, so a leak is hard to notice.

examples.ko: 무색무취의 물은 마셔도 맛이 거의 안 나요.
examples.en: Colorless, odorless water has almost no taste when you drink it.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 무색무취한 느낌이라는 평을 들었어요.
examples.en: That singer was said to come across as bland and characterless.

examples.ko: 약품이 무색무취여서 냄새로는 구별할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The chemical is colorless and odorless, so you can't tell it apart by smell.

examples.ko: 무색무취한 디자인보다 특징이 있는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer something with character over a bland design.
It was a colorless, odorless liquid, so I thought it was water.

explain: 가스나 액체 같은 물질을 설명할 때도 쓰고, 개성이 없는 사람이나 작품을 비유할 때도 써요. 비유로 쓰면 '밋밋하다', '개성이 없다'는 약간 아쉬운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes substances such as gases and liquids, and also works as a metaphor for people or works with no personality. In the metaphorical sense it suggests something bland or lacking character, a little disappointing.

examples.ko: 폭우로 인명 피해는 없었지만 물적 피해는 컸어요.
examples.en: There were no casualties from the heavy rain, but the property damage was big.
The police are looking for physical evidence.

examples.ko: 회사가 어려워서 인적, 물적 자원이 많이 부족해요.
examples.en: The company is struggling, so human and material resources are very short.

examples.ko: 이 사고로 물적 손해가 얼마나 났는지 조사해요.
examples.en: They are investigating how much material loss this accident caused.
To start a business, you also need a material base.

examples.ko: 정부가 피해 지역에 물적 지원을 약속했어요.
examples.en: The government promised material support for the affected area.

explain: 관형사라서 뒤에 꼭 명사가 와요. 물적 피해, 물적 증거, 물적 자원처럼 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '인적'이고, 뉴스의 사고 보도에서 '인적·물적 피해'로 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a determiner, so a noun must follow, as in 물적 피해, 물적 증거 and 물적 자원. Its counterpart is '인적', and the two often appear together as '인적·물적 피해' in accident news.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 상업성이 너무 강해서 아쉬웠어요.
examples.en: This movie was too commercial, which was disappointing.
Considering its commercial appeal, this plan is risky.

examples.ko: 작품성도 좋고 상업성도 있어서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: It has artistic merit and commercial appeal, so it's very popular.

examples.ko: 상업성에 너무 치우치면 팬들이 떠날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lean too much on commercial appeal, fans may leave.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 상업성보다 예술성을 더 중요하게 생각해요.
examples.en: That director values artistry more than commercial appeal.
Its commercial appeal is low, but it's a meaningful work.

explain: 영화, 음악, 책처럼 작품이 돈이 되는 정도를 말할 때 써요. '작품성', '예술성'과 같이 놓고 비교하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to how profitable a work such as a film, song, or book is. It is often set side by side with '작품성' (artistic merit) or '예술성' (artistry).

examples.ko: 이 가수의 노래는 서정성이 풍부해서 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: This singer's songs are rich in lyricism, so they put my mind at ease.

examples.ko: 서정성 짙은 시를 읽으며 가을을 보냈어요.
examples.en: I spent autumn reading deeply lyrical poems.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 화려한 장면보다 서정성으로 사랑받았어요.
examples.en: That film was loved for its lyricism rather than flashy scenes.

examples.ko: 소설에 서정성을 더하니 분위기가 훨씬 부드러워졌어요.
examples.en: Adding lyricism to the novel made the mood much softer.
I like works with more narrative than lyricism.

examples.ko: 이 시집은 서정성과 사회적 메시지를 함께 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This poetry collection holds both lyricism and a social message.

explain: 시, 노래, 영화, 그림이 감정을 부드럽고 섬세하게 느끼게 할 때 '서정성이 있다', '서정성이 풍부하다', '서정성이 짙다'처럼 말해요. 이야기 전개가 중심인 '서사성'과 비교해서 많이 써요.
explain_en: When a poem, song, film or painting makes you feel emotion softly and delicately, you say '서정성이 있다', '서정성이 풍부하다' or '서정성이 짙다'. It is often compared with '서사성', which centers on the development of the story.

examples.ko: 부품의 소형화 덕분에 휴대폰이 훨씬 가벼워졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the miniaturization of parts, phones have become much lighter.
These days the competition to make home appliances smaller is fierce.
As miniaturization progressed, laptops got thinner too.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 카메라 소형화 기술로 유명해요.
examples.en: This company is famous for its camera miniaturization technology.

examples.ko: 1인 가구가 늘어서 아파트 평수의 소형화가 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: With more single-person households, the shrinking size of apartments is noticeable.
They say there is a limit to shrinking semiconductors.

explain: 반대말은 '대형화'예요. 기계, 부품, 기술, 집 크기 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 그냥 작아졌다고 말할 때는 '작아지다'를 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '대형화' (enlargement). It often appears when talking about machines, parts, technology and the size of homes; for something simply getting small, people say '작아지다'.

examples.en: These days I'm suffering from nervous gastritis.

examples.ko: 신경성 두통이라서 약이 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: It's a stress-related headache, so medicine doesn't work well.
The doctor said it was stress-related.
Every exam I get a nervous stomachache.

examples.ko: 신경성 소화불량에는 잠을 푹 자는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For nervous indigestion, it's good to get plenty of sleep.
These symptoms are quite likely stress-related.

explain: 뒤에 병 이름이나 증상을 붙여 '신경성 위염', '신경성 두통'처럼 써요. 몸에 큰 이상이 있어서가 아니라 스트레스나 마음의 긴장이 원인일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It goes before an illness or symptom, as in '신경성 위염' or '신경성 두통'. It is used when the cause is stress or mental tension rather than a clear physical problem.

examples.en: This document has to be kept permanently.

examples.ko: 사고로 시력을 영구히 잃을 수도 있대요.
examples.en: They say you could permanently lose your eyesight in an accident.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 영구히 문을 닫기로 했어요.
examples.en: That shop decided to close for good.
This promise will be kept forever.

examples.ko: 사진을 영구히 남기고 싶어서 액자에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to keep the photo permanently, so I put it in a frame.

examples.ko: 영구히 사용할 수 있는 이용권을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pass that can be used permanently.

explain: '영원히'와 비슷하지만 영구히는 보관, 정지, 권리, 규칙처럼 딱딱한 사무적인 이야기에 어울려요. 사랑이나 이별 같은 감정을 말할 때는 '영원히'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대되는 말은 '일시적으로'예요.
explain_en: It is similar to '영원히', but 영구히 fits formal, practical topics such as storage, suspension, rights and rules. For feelings like love or parting, '영원히' sounds more natural. The opposite is '일시적으로' (temporarily).

examples.en: That singer is highly regarded for her musicality.

examples.ko: 인기만 있는 게 아니라 음악성도 인정받았어요.
examples.en: He is not only popular but also recognized for his musicality.

examples.ko: 이 앨범은 음악성보다 대중성을 더 신경 썼어요.
examples.en: This album cares more about popular appeal than musicality.
Is musicality something you are born with, or is it developed?
Critics rated his musicality highly.

examples.ko: 음악성 있는 연주자와 함께 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with a musically gifted player.

explain: 사람과 작품에 모두 쓰고, 칭찬할 때는 '음악성이 좋다', '음악성이 뛰어나다'처럼 말해요. '대중성'과 짝으로 나오는 때가 많아요. 가수나 연주자를 평가하는 글이나 방송에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is used for both people and works, and in praise you say '음악성이 좋다' or '음악성이 뛰어나다'. It often appears as a pair with '대중성' (popular appeal). You hear it in reviews and broadcasts that evaluate singers or players.

examples.en: The pharmacist made up my cold medicine.
They prepare the medicine according to the prescription.
The herbal doctor is preparing the herbal medicine.

examples.ko: 약을 조제하는 데 십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about ten minutes to prepare the medicine.

examples.ko: 이 약은 약국에서만 조제할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can only be made up at a pharmacy.

examples.ko: 어제 조제한 약을 아직 안 먹었어요.
examples.en: I haven't taken the medicine that was prepared yesterday.

explain: '만들다'와 달리 약을 처방에 맞게 섞어 만들 때 써요. 약국에서 '조제해 드릴게요'라는 말을 자주 들어요. 음식에는 거의 쓰지 않고 '만들다'를 써요.
explain_en: Unlike 만들다, 조제하다 is for mixing and making up medicine to match a prescription. At a pharmacy you often hear '조제해 드릴게요'. For food, people almost always say 만들다 instead.

examples.en: There is a parking lot in the lower part of the building.
The lower part of the bridge is old, so they inspect it.
Please open the lower cover of the machine.
Please put only documents in the bottom drawer.
The news reached even the lower levels of the organization.
The bottom part got cut off in the photo.

explain: '하부'는 '아래 부분'을 딱딱하게 말하는 단어예요. 일상에서는 '아래'나 '밑'을 더 많이 쓰고, 설명서나 공사·조직 이야기에서 '하부'를 써요. 반대말은 '상부'예요.
explain_en: 하부 is a stiff way to say 'the lower part'. In daily talk people use 아래 or 밑, while 하부 appears in manuals, construction, and organization talk. Its opposite is 상부.

examples.en: A free lecture is held at the district office hall.
Let's meet in front of the village hall.
The student hall has a cafeteria and a snack shop.
That hall is old, so it's being repaired.
I took the bus to the citizens' hall.
The neighbors cleaned the hall together.

explain: 모임·행사·강연을 위해 지은 건물 이름에 붙어요. '시민회관', '학생회관', '마을회관'처럼 앞에 누가 쓰는지 붙이고, 영어의 '홀'이나 '센터'와 비슷하지만 한국에서는 공공 건물이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It attaches to the names of buildings made for meetings, events, and lectures, with the users in front, as in '시민회관', '학생회관', and '마을회관'. It is close to English 'hall' or 'center', but in Korea it has a public-building feel.
